title: Burial of the Dead
lead: In the Bible, burying the dead is a duty of love and honor, and to lie unburied is a curse. Abraham buys a burial cave, Joseph's bones are carried out of Egypt, and the law forbids leaving even an executed man's body hanging overnight. Jesus is buried with care by his friends. Christian teaching on burial and cremation grew from these stories and from hope in the resurrection of the body.

sections.b: Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah (Genesis 23), and the patriarchs ask to be buried there (Genesis 49:29–32). Joseph makes Israel swear to carry his bones to the land (Genesis 50:25; Exodus 13:19; Joshua 24:32). The law says a hanged body must be buried the same day (Deuteronomy 21:22–23). The men of Jabesh-gilead risk their lives to bury Saul (1 Samuel 31:11–13), and Rizpah guards her sons' bodies (2 Samuel 21:10–14). Being left for the birds is a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26; Jeremiah 16:4). Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bury Jesus (John 19:38–42), and Paul uses burial as a picture of baptism (Romans 6:4).
